recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7678 unless a future work group decision changes the Attachment data/url/contentType rule itself.
issue_request: FHIR-7678 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 FHIR-I clarification reporting that Attachment.contentType narrative said the element SHALL always be populated while the formal definition made it optional; the approved resolution was to adjust the note so it was clearer.
initial_application: No FHIR-7678-tagged source commit was found in git history, and the Jira comment says the change was already applied. The same Attachment.contentType conflict was applied in SVN-backed git commit 5ae1eebfcac2835ff22fdbbc1cdfb452b33ab838 (#7878, svn r5937), which replaced the unconditional SHALL narrative with conditional wording requiring contentType only when an Attachment contains data and permitting it for url-only attachments.
additional_context: FHIR-7878 is the tightly related Published issue for the same conflict and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 9457a59e7f6de445e9a013220c47cd1d43d9d064, so it was not republished. source/fhir.ini keeps Attachment in the active [types] list, routes datatypes through datatypes.html by default, and marks Attachment normative.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active Attachment narrative, cardinality, and invariant already express the clarification requested by FHIR-7678: contentType is not universally mandatory, but is mandatory when inline data is present.

related_jiras.note: Published issue for the same Attachment.contentType documentation conflict; already audited on the combined branch and not decided again here.
Historical change that made Attachment.contentType optional except when inline data is present, establishing the formal rule that the narrative now matches.
